note: Five separate checks at a cylinder-measured 15 mL (not reused/estimated -- user re-measured each time, draining and re-pouring fresh before the last one), each visually confirmed by the user as 'the detected line looks right' against the real liquid edge at the time. boundary_y spread 43px across the first four (~10-12 mL equivalent at this region's local slope); the 5th (fresh re-pour) landed on exactly the same value as the 4th (530, confirmed on a second /status query). Conclusion: the static detector itself is not repeatable at this operating point under the current lighting/ROI, independent of pour accuracy or single-frame visual plausibility -- a genuine finding, not a one-off error. Documented as a limitation; the ruler-based records/calibration_table.json (RMSE 0.589 mL) remains the table actually used.
Two separate checks at a cylinder-measured 25 mL. 26px spread -- consistent with the same non-repeatability pattern found at 15 mL, at a different volume/region of the ROI.

First two checks (one at 35 mL, one at a re-poured 37 mL) both locked onto the same value (486) -- the structural bulb/cone edge, matching the 30 mL point almost exactly (487). This third check, a fresh re-pour at 35 mL, instead landed near where the table would predict (interpolated ~475.5 between 30 mL/487 and 40 mL/464), off by only ~8px. So the failure mode here isn't a hard permanent lock -- the detector sometimes finds a position close to correct and sometimes snaps to the false edge, at the same nominal volume. Same conclusion as the 15/25 mL repeatability checks (not repeatable under current ROI/lighting), different symptom (bimodal/intermittent here vs. continuous spread there).

EXPOSURE_US raised from the 25000 default to 45000 (ROI brightness ~100-120 -> ~136-157/255), same ROI/focus otherwise. Four fresh cylinder-measured 35 mL pours (drained and re-poured each time, not reused) all landed within 2px of each other (472, 473, 472, 471) -- versus 43px spread (15 mL) and the 486/486/467 bimodal lock (35/37 mL) seen before this change. Conclusion: insufficient exposure, not a hard geometric/ROI problem, was the dominant cause of the earlier non-repeatability. Camera-direct pixel_row calibration should be re-attempted at this exposure level before concluding it's unusable -- the earlier 'use the ruler table instead' recommendation may need revisiting once this is confirmed across the other volumes (10/20/30/40/15/25) too.
